title: Mocomanto, Shinnecock Sachem
summary: Mocomanto was a mid-seventeenth-century Shinnecock leader named among the Native signers of the December 13, 1640 Southampton deed.
content:
Mocomanto was a mid-seventeenth-century Shinnecock leader named among the Native signers of the December 13, 1640 Southampton deed. The surviving record preserves only this narrow view of his leadership and does not establish his birth or death dates.

The document is central to colonial Southampton history, but it preserves only a narrow view of Mocomanto's life and leadership.1

Historical Context

The 1640 deed places Mocomanto in early Shinnecock and English negotiations over the Southampton landscape.12

Because the surviving evidence is brief, this biography centers the documented deed role and does not add unsupported family history, dates of birth or death, or claims about later leadership.1

References

  1. George R. Howell, The Early History of Southampton, L. I., New York, p. 451.
  2. Gaynell Stone, The Shinnecock Indians: A Culture History, p. 67.
  3. Donna Barron, The Long Island Indians and Their New England Ancestors.
why_this_matters: Mocomanto belongs in public Southampton history because English settlement narratives often obscure the Shinnecock leaders whose land, diplomacy, and signatures made those colonial records possible.
